questions.text: A procurement team has identified that staff spend significant time answering the same procurement policy questions from other departments. What should they do to address this inefficiency?

answers.text: Issue a solicitation for an AI vendor immediately to save time
Ask IT to build a custom solution since off-the-shelf tools won't understand their specific policies
Survey staff about which AI tools they are most comfortable using
Conduct a discovery process to map current workflows, identify root causes, and assess whether their policy documents are organized and current enough to support an AI tool

questions.text: A procurement director wants to launch an AI pilot but has not yet secured support from IT or legal. What is the most likely consequence of proceeding without their involvement?

answers.text: The pilot will succeed faster since fewer stakeholders means fewer delays
IT and legal can be brought in after the pilot to review outcomes and provide retroactive approval
The pilot will be less innovative since IT tends to be risk-averse
The pilot may stall due to unresolved questions about tool approval, data access, acceptable use, and liability

questions.text: Green Bell Province wants to measure the success of their new AI-assisted procurement training tool. Which of the following would be the most useful set of KPIs?

answers.text: Number of AI prompts submitted per week and average response time
Number of staff who completed AI training and total cost of the tool license
Reduction in time procurement staff spend answering policy questions and decrease in policy-related errors by other departments
Percentage of procurement documents reviewed by AI and number of hallucinations detected
